name: West District and Calligraphy Greenway
tagline: The cultural strip, museums and the best cafes in the city
description: The central district running along the Calligraphy Greenway, a linear park connecting the art museum to the science museum, lined with independent cafes, galleries and the city's best restaurants. It is the most pleasant part of Taichung to walk and the most sought after to live in.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the museums, the park and the cafes on the doorstep
pros: The linear park and both major museums on foot
The best independent cafes and restaurants in the city
Genuinely walkable, which much of Taichung is not
cons: The highest rents in the city
No metro station in parts of the district

name: Xitun and the Seventh District
tagline: The new centre, with the opera house and the towers
description: The planned northwestern expansion holding the Taichung Metropolitan Opera House designed by Toyo Ito, the department stores and the newest apartment towers. It is the city's modern showpiece: wide streets, new buildings, high rents and the best building infrastructure in Taichung.
bestFor: Stays wanting a new apartment and the opera house district
pros: The opera house, department stores and parks nearby
MRT green line through the district
cons: Car and scooter dependent in parts

name: Fengjia
tagline: Around the night market, Taiwan's largest, and the cheapest rooms
description: The student district around Feng Chia University, whose night market is one of the biggest in Taiwan and runs late every night of the week. Rents here are the lowest in the city, the food is exceptional and trivially cheap, and it is loud from evening until well after midnight.
bestFor: Budget stays that want the night market downstairs and do not mind the noise
pros: Taiwan's largest night market on the doorstep
cons: Genuinely loud every night until late
Crowded streets and heavy scooter traffic

name: Central District and Taichung Station
tagline: The old downtown, faded and slowly coming back
description: The original city centre around the restored Japanese-era railway station, with the old markets, the Miyahara building and streets of shophouses that emptied when the city moved west and are now being reoccupied. It is the cheapest central district and the most interesting architecturally.
bestFor: Budget stays that want the station, the old markets and the historic buildings
pros: Restored station and the old market quarter
Trains and buses in every direction
cons: Still visibly run down in parts
Fewer good restaurants than the west
Streets around the station are less comfortable late

name: Beitun and Dakeng
tagline: The northeastern edge, where the hiking trails start
description: The northeastern districts running up to Dakeng, a scenic area of hills inside the city limits with a well-known network of wooden hiking trails. Housing is a mix of newer complexes and older residential streets, cheaper than the west, with hot springs and the trails a short ride away.
bestFor: Stays where hiking from the city edge matters more than the cafes
pros: Dakeng hiking trails within the city limits
Cleaner air and greener than the plain
Rents well below the western districts
cons: Twenty to thirty minutes into the centre
Scooter or car needed for most things
